hooks.text: A comet once shone so brightly it was studied in broad daylight.
Comet West plunged within thirty million kilometers of the Sun in 1976.
Comet West reached a peak apparent magnitude of minus three.

title: The Comet Seen in Broad Daylight
description: Discover Comet West, the dazzling 1976 sungrazer that split into four pieces and shone bright enough to be studied in broad daylight.

beats.text: A comet once shone so brightly astronomers studied it in broad daylight.
beats.visual: Telescope photograph of Comet West showing its bright head and tail, 1976

beats.text: Discovered photographically by astronomer Richard M. West on August tenth, 1975, the magnificent sungrazer plummeted toward our star.
beats.visual: European Southern Observatory La Silla Schmidt telescope, 1975

beats.text: By February twenty-fifth, 1976, the cosmic visitor raced within exactly thirty million kilometers of the Sun.
beats.visual: Diagram of a comet orbit showing perihelion and trajectory

beats.text: Intense solar heating pushed its peak apparent magnitude to minus three, easily rivaling Venus.
beats.visual: Artist concept illustration of a long period comet nucleus fragmenting

beats.text: Observers watched in absolute amazement from February twenty-fifth to twenty-seventh as the dazzling object was clearly viewed under a full sun.
beats.visual: Telescope image of Comet West bright head and tail in daylight

beats.text: Brutal tidal forces soon shattered the wandering ice block into four distinct pieces out in space.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a comet nucleus fracturing into multiple fragments

beats.text: This daytime record proves comets can brilliantly outshine the daytime sky.
beats.visual: Telescope image of Comet West showing its massive dust tail
